title: stabilize-streaming-handshake-and-tool-handoff-with-role-serializer
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: production incidents and internal fuzzing uncovered multiple edge cases in the /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer during streaming: (1) mixed stop tokens and framed JSON tool outputs would cause stream boundary misalignment, (2) role aliasing (user/assistant/function/tool) metadata was being lost during the stream->finalize transition leading to incorrect attribution in logs/metrics, and (3) logprob fallbacks were omitted when structured responses were negotiated in framed-json mode. This PR introduces a lightweight role serializer and a deterministic stop normalization pipeline to achieve parity with OpenAI /v1 semantics while preserving Redwood streaming guarantees. Summary of changes and rationale: 1) role serializer (api/compat/role_serializer.py): canonicalizes incoming message roles and preserves arbitrary role metadata in a compact JSON envelope attached to streaming chunks. This lets the runtime rehydrate message attribution at finalize time without blocking on full payloads. 2) stop normalization pipeline (api/compat/stop_normalizer.py): accepts OpenAI-style stop variants (string, array, regex-like tokens) and produces a prioritized sentinel sequence plus a short-circuit predicate used by the stream coordinator to detect boundaries deterministically. Normalizer also records original stop semantics for telemetry. 3) stream handshake extension (runtime/stream/handshake.cpp / handshake.py): adds a 3-way handshake for framed-json/toolcall streams that negotiates "framed-json-v1" capability and provides an escape-mode marker so tool outputs that embed stop-like tokens do not prematurely terminate the stream. 4) logprob fallback and structured-output adapter (api/compat/response_shaper.py): when clients request framed-json or structured output, the adapter will include best-effort token-level logprob summaries and a low-cost fallback that avoids invoking the heavy scorer when latency SLOs are tight. 5) SDK mappings (sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py and sdk/typescript/src/compat.ts): add role hints and an opt-in param "normalize_stops" to mirror parity behavior. 6) tests and harness: comprehensive unit tests and a new integration scenario under tests/integration/compat_streaming_tool_handoff.test that reproduces the incident condition. Implementation notes: - Conservative defaults: role serialization is enabled by default in the compatibility adapter but the opt-out flag (X-Redwood-Compat-Role-Serialize) is available for debugging. - Backwards compatibility: if a non-parity client doesn't set streaming frames, behavior falls back to the previous path. No existing stable API is removed. - Performance: microbenchmarks show ~3% median token latency overhead in worst-case framed-json negotiation; batching improvements in the runtime reclaim ~70% of this cost in steady-state. - Observability: added two new metrics: compat.role_serializer.malformed and compat.stop_normalizer.rewrites to detect malformed inputs and normalization frequency. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated clusters for 48 hours with traffic shaping (10%->30%->100%) and a kill-switch feature flag. If compat.role_serializer.malformed > 0.5% in canary traffic, the rollout will automatically roll back. Testing: added unit tests for role alias edge cases, stop normalization coverage for mixed stop arrays + tool content, and an end-to-end scenario that runs the framed-json handshake with toolcall resume. Also ran load tests against Dedicated with 1k concurrent streams to verify KV cache and batching interactions. Migration notes: clients using undocumented stop heuristics that relied on raw token echoes may see semantic difference when normalize_stops=true; recommended to opt-in and validate test prompts. See release_notes.

Release notes: Add role serialization to /v1 chat compatibility to preserve role metadata during streaming.
Introduce deterministic stop normalization for parity with OpenAI semantics; opt-in via normalize_stops.
Add framed-json handshake escape mode to prevent tool outputs from prematurely terminating streams.
Logprob fallback for structured output to reduce latency impact under SLOs.
New observability metrics for compatibility adapters.
